messages.author: fee7d8264533fcfd
messages.subject: Questions about the effective plot
parts:
Hi, I have two ‘positive’ marker from a QTL analysis in F1 population. one allele (lm x ll)  is heterozygous in female and homozygous on male type, while the other (hk x hk) is heterozygous on both parents.

When I looked at the effective plots, it gave four genotype (AC, BC, AD, BD) for both of the markers. I am confused here, shouldn't it be two genotypes for the first allele and three genotypes for the second allele as far as the recombination goes?

Thanks.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Questions about the effective plot
parts:
With phase-known four-way crosses in R/qtl, we use the multiple linked markers on a chromosome to infer each individual’s genotype. The parents are taken to be AB x CD, and so the offspring have genotype AC, AD, BC, or BD. 

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Questions about the effective plot
parts:
I can't advise you on how to proceed without knowing what it is you're trying to do, or what you are concerned about.

In R/qtl, the only function that provides percent variance explained by a QTL is fitqtl(). You need to first run makeqtl() to create a QTL object.

karl
